item.description: AI-based assistants or "agents" -- autonomous programs that have access to the user's computer, files, online services and can automate virtually any task -- are growing in popularity with developers and IT workers. item.title: [general] Cloudflare moves up its post-quantum deadline as researchers narrow the path to Q-Day
item.description: <p>Cloudflare announced it is targeting 2029 to complete post-quantum security across its entire product suite, including post-quantum authentication. The company is following a revised roadmap that Google also adopted after announcing that it had improved the quantum algorithm used to break elliptic curve cryptography. Google stopped short of publishing the algorithm, disclosing only a zero-knowledge proof of its existence. The same day, a company called Oratomic published a resource estimate for breaking RSA-2048 and P-256 &#8230; <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/04/07/cloudflare-post-quantum-authentication/" rel="nofollow">More <span class="meta-nav">&#8594;</span></a></p> <p>The post <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/04/07/cloudflare-post-quantum-authentication/">Cloudflare moves up its post-quantum deadline as researchers narrow the path to Q-Day</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com">Help Net Security</a>.</p>

item.title: [general] GitHub Copilot CLI gets a second-opinion feature built on cross-model review
item.description: <p>Coding agents make decisions in sequence: a plan is drafted, implemented, then tested. Any error introduced early compounds as subsequent steps build on the same flawed assumption. Self-reflection is a recognized mitigation technique, and one GitHub Copilot already supports, but a model reviewing its own output is still constrained by the same training data and blind spots that produced it. item.title: [general] Google study finds LLMs are embedded at every stage of abuse detection
item.description: <p>Online platforms are running large language models at every stage of LLM content moderation, from generating training data to auditing their own systems for bias. Researchers at Google mapped how this is happening across what the authors call the Abuse Detection Lifecycle, a four-stage framework covering labeling, detection, review and appeals, and auditing. Earlier moderation systems, built on models like BERT and RoBERTa fine-tuned on static hate-speech datasets, could identify explicit slurs with reasonable accuracy. &#8230; <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/04/07/google-llm-content-moderation/" rel="nofollow">More <span class="meta-nav">&#8594;</span></a></p> <p>The post <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/04/07/google-llm-content-moderation/">Google study finds LLMs are embedded at every stage of abuse detection</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com">Help Net Security</a>.</p>

item.title: [general] Residential proxies make a mockery of IP-based defenses
item.description: <p>Attack traffic moved through ordinary home and mobile connections in ways that limited the usefulness of IP reputation on its own. GreyNoise observed 4 billion malicious sessions during a 90-day period and described activity that appeared indistinguishable from normal user traffic at the network level. Residential proxies routed traffic through consumer broadband, mobile data, and small-business connections. These same IP ranges were used by employees, customers, and partners, which made it difficult to separate malicious &#8230; <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/04/06/residential-proxy-attack-traffic-ip-reputation-enterprise-security/" rel="nofollow">More <span class="meta-nav">&#8594;</span></a></p> <p>The post <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/04/06/residential-proxy-attack-traffic-ip-reputation-enterprise-security/">Residential proxies make a mockery of IP-based defenses</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com">Help Net Security</a>.</p>
